Of those, 1 lie on a cell where a plan was found, i.e. where the INDUCTION channel this session's work acts through was actually open; the rest are pre-induction explore reordering and evidence only that SOMETHING in the span changed, not that the induction fixes did. The mechanism is named and reproducible on ['vc33'] -- see vc33_goal_predicate_regression_replicated_across_two_probes.

base_arm_noise_floor_added_on_review.arm: baseb (8441055c0 again, same worktree, same seeds, same config as base)
base_arm_noise_floor_added_on_review.scope: run on the four cells that carried the attributable finding, not all twelve. Those are the only cells whose CLASSIFICATION a base-side floor can change, and the grid had already spent its wall budget. A cell outside this set has no base-side determinism witness and is reported as such rather than assumed.
base_arm_noise_floor_added_on_review.the_hypothesis_this_tested_and_its_OUTCO: HYPOTHESIS (from review): base is the noisy arm, so the class-1 explore reorderings are base perturbing against itself and the attributable count collapses from 4 to 1. It was a serious hypothesis with real supporting evidence, quoted below. REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT: base vs baseb came back IDENTICAL on all four cells -- tu93 28/28, tr87 27/27, tn36 31/31, vc33 14/14, zero divergences, base-arm floor 0/4. So the base arm repeats itself byte-for-byte on exactly the cells that carry the finding, and the attributable count stands at 4. Settled by running the arm rather than by arguing about it, which is the point: the review was right that the assumption was unlicensed, and wrong about which way it would fall.
base_arm_noise_floor_added_on_review.the_supporting_evidence_that_made_the_hy: the base worktree's own results/proto_just_explore_budget_scan.json documents this codebase's explore path as nondeterministic across fresh processes, in its own words: 'ar25@2000 with the SAME seed in three FRESH processes gave atfl=362, then 153, then no-solve. The residual nondeterminism is dict/set iteration order in the graph explorer's frontier (untested_edges from hash-keyed structures, PYTHONHASHSEED randomized per process).' Verified by reading that file directly. probe_cell.py does NOT pin PYTHONHASHSEED, so that channel is open on both arms of this grid too.
base_arm_noise_floor_added_on_review.why_it_did_not_bite_here_stated_as_a_lim: the documented nondeterminism is in the just-explore GRAPH EXPLORER's frontier. This probe runs the E3AgentPolicy explore stream at budget=60 with explore_budget=24, and on these four cells that stream is evidently reproducible across processes. That is an empirical result about THESE cells at THIS budget, not a proof that the channel is closed: a different game, a longer budget, or a path that reaches the graph explorer could still expose it. Any future grid should pin PYTHONHASHSEED on both arms rather than rely on this holding.
base_arm_noise_floor_added_on_review.why_this_field_exists: the grid's original 'A/A floor' was head-vs-headb ONLY. Every A/B pair is base-vs-head and holds exactly ONE base run, unreplicated -- so a 0/6 head-arm floor proves HEAD repeats itself and says NOTHING about BASE. If base is the noisy arm, the perturbations credited to the treatment are the base arm perturbing against itself. That is not a hypothetical: 4f7e5f55a changes the search's dedup KEY, exactly the kind of change that can STABILISE iteration order, so a determinism ASYMMETRY between the arms is the EXPECTED consequence of the treatment. probe_cell.py also never pins PYTHONHASHSEED, so str/bytes hashing is randomised per process on both arms. Measured rather than assumed.

named_in_the_question: f9a458e87 win-state positive example + 5 input-side fixes

defect_1_census_blind_to_never_started_c.mechanism: the CLI builds its cell census from FILENAMES present on disk (the union of the two arms' files). A game that has not started on EITHER arm contributes no file, so it is not in the census, so it is not counted as MISSING. `preflight_verdict`'s INCONCLUSIVE guard is driven by `counts[MISSING]`, so with no MISSING cells it concludes the grid is finished and returns REFUSE.

minimal_reproduction_run_in_this_session.cli_result: VERDICT: REFUSE, exit code 1, counts {'IDENTICAL': 1, 'PERTURBED': 0, 'MISSING': 0} -- note MISSING is ZERO, not 11
minimal_reproduction_run_in_this_session.conclusion: identical data, OPPOSITE verdicts, and the only difference is whether never-started cells appear in the census. Exit code 1 means a caller scripting on the exit status reads an unfinished probe as a refusal.
minimal_reproduction_run_in_this_session.setup: copy ONE game's three cells (base/head/headb for ft09) into an empty directory and point the CLI at it, while the planned grid is 12 games

defect_1_census_blind_to_never_started_c.observed: `scripts/treatment_activation_preflight.py --cells <partial grid> --control base --treatment head --replicate headb` reported VERDICT: REFUSE on a grid that was still running, with 9 of 12 games not yet started.
defect_1_census_blind_to_never_started_c.suggested_fix: the CLI should take the planned cell list explicitly (or infer MISSING from `--planned-n-cells` minus the census) so that never-started cells are counted as MISSING rather than being invisible.
defect_1_census_blind_to_never_started_c.why_it_matters: REFUSE is a FINDING ('no outcome of this grid can reach alpha'); INCONCLUSIVE is 'the probe has not decided yet'. The module's own docstring says INCONCLUSIVE exists precisely so that 'a probe stopped early for an unrelated reason' cannot be laundered into a finding that the treatment is inert. That protection is defeated one layer up, at the census, where the module cannot see it. This artifact avoids the bug only because its builder enumerates the full planned game list rather than the directory.

defect_2_projection_has_no_lower_confide.mechanism: `preflight_verdict` projects `rate * planned` using the POINT estimate of the perturbation rate, with no lower bound. At n_usable=2 the rate 0.5 has a 95% interval of roughly [0.01, 0.99], so the projection is dominated by sampling error -- and here it lands exactly on the threshold, so the PASS is decided by a single cell.
defect_2_projection_has_no_lower_confide.observed: the same partial grid -- ONE perturbed cell out of TWO usable observations -- returns VERDICT: PASS when given `--planned-n-cells 12`, on the basis `projected 6.0 attributable cells at planned n=12 vs 6 required`.
defect_2_projection_has_no_lower_confide.suggested_fix: project the LOWER confidence bound of the rate (e.g. Wilson at 95%) rather than the point estimate, and/or refuse to project at all below some minimum n_usable, returning INCONCLUSIVE instead.

what_the_fix_would_change_computed_in_th.note: point-estimate projection to n=12 vs Wilson-95%-lower projection to n=12, for the same observed counts. The point estimate PASSES every one of these; the lower bound passes none. The 0.5 rate projects to exactly 6.0 -- the threshold -- at ANY n, which is why the defect is invisible until you vary n.

defect_2_projection_has_no_lower_confide.why_it_matters: a PASS licenses spending hours on the full grid. Licensing it off one observation is the same over-reading of thin data the module was built to prevent, in the one code path that says yes.

defect_3_TAUTOLOGY_false_positive_on_a_b.CONFIRMED_BY_THE_FLAG_CLEARING_ITSELF: the cleanest possible proof, and it arrived without touching a single number. On the 4-game and 6-game builds the A/B arm had ZERO truncation-affected cells, charitable ceiling == strict ceiling, and the flag fired. On the FINAL 8-game build su15's A/B came back TRUNCATION_ONLY, so charitable = strict + 1 = 5 vs strict 4, the two p-values separated (0.0625 vs 0.125), and adversarial_verify now reports '0 flagged'. The flag appeared and disappeared exactly as the slack term went 0 -> 1, which is what a structural identity does and what a real two-metric bug would not.
defect_3_TAUTOLOGY_false_positive_on_a_b.consequence_if_not_fixed: this artifact carries a CRITICAL adversarial flag, so per the fabrication gate it must NOT be aggregated into a capstone or headline until the operator either applies the carve-out or accepts the note. Stated plainly rather than worked around.
defect_3_TAUTOLOGY_false_positive_on_a_b.it_is_systematic_not_a_one_off_coinciden: the flag fired on the 4-game build with both p-values at 0.5 (strict ceiling 2) and again on the 6-game build with both at 0.25 (strict ceiling 3). It will fire at EVERY value of the ceiling, because the two quantities are the same function of the same number whenever the A/B truncation count is 0. That is the signature of a structural false positive rather than a coincidence that happened to land on a round number.
defect_3_TAUTOLOGY_false_positive_on_a_b.observed: `scripts/adversarial_verify.py` raised CRITICAL TAUTOLOGY on the 4-game and 6-game builds of this artifact: 'best_reachable_p_charitable and best_reachable_p_strict agree to >5 sig figs. Two distinct metrics matching this precisely is more likely a bug than a finding.' Exit code 1, so the fabrication gate would have quarantined it. Stated in the PAST tense: the flag is NOT standing on the final build -- see CONFIRMED_BY_THE_FLAG_CLEARING_ITSELF below, which is why the defect is reported as structural rather than as a live blocker.
defect_3_TAUTOLOGY_false_positive_on_a_b.suggested_fix: carve out pairs where one metric is a documented monotone bound on the other and the artifact records the slack term as zero. Mechanically: if a pair matches (X_strict, X_charitable) naming AND the artifact's n_truncation_affected (or an explicitly named slack field) is 0, skip. Keep it gated on the slack actually being zero so a genuine copy-paste bug between two independent metrics is still flagged.
defect_3_TAUTOLOGY_false_positive_on_a_b.what_i_did_NOT_do: I did not perturb, round, or drop either p-value to clear the flag. Altering a number to satisfy a fabrication detector is the exact anti-pattern the Verifier Authenticity Discipline names (score-capping to dodge IMPLAUSIBLE_PERFECT). Both fields are reported as computed, a `methodology_note` documents the identity, and the flag is left standing for the operator to judge.
defect_3_TAUTOLOGY_false_positive_on_a_b.why_it_belongs_in_the_same_class_as_the_: check_tautology already carves out identifier/seed fields, chance-floor 0.5 score pairs, small shared-denominator ARC rates, declared control-vs-treatment honest nulls, and small-integer count coincidences -- every one of them a 'these two are equal for structural reasons' case. A strict-vs-charitable BOUND pair is the same class and is not yet covered.
defect_3_TAUTOLOGY_false_positive_on_a_b.why_it_is_a_FALSE_POSITIVE: the charitable ceiling is DEFINED in preflight_verdict as `ceiling_charitable = ceiling_strict + n_truncation_affected`. Whenever that slack term is 0 the two ceilings are the same NUMBER by construction and the two p-values are the same function of that number -- not two distinct measurements, but a bound and the thing it bounds with zero slack. That is the condition under which the flag fires, and it is a property of the DEFINITION, not of any particular run. CORRECTED 2026-07-30: an earlier version of this field asserted 'the A/B arm of this grid has n_truncation_affected = 0', which the artifact's own preflight_verdict_full contradicted on the final build (n_truncation_affected = 1, su15). Stale prose from a 6-game build was doing load-bearing work in the argument that dismissed a CRITICAL flag, which is exactly the kind of drift that makes a dismissal untrustworthy. See methodology_note for the computed values.

defects_found_in_the_instrument_while_us.not_a_defect: the CLI's byte-level disagreement with this probe's external trace encoding is NOT a defect -- the two encodings differ by design and the semantic comparison agrees action-for-action (see instrument_cross_check_external_vs_head_native).
defects_found_in_the_instrument_while_us.why_this_is_here: these are bugs in the thing that DECIDES whether other experiments count, which CLAUDE.md's QA-Layer Authenticity Discipline names as a class needing more care than an ordinary bug. Both were found by running the shipped CLI against this grid and comparing it to the analysis in this artifact. NOT fixed here -- reported for the operator to act on.

_summary.what_this_means: a cell listed in cells_where_NEITHER_aa_arm_crossed_cards_but_the_ab_did has no within-cell cross-card determinism witness: its treatment comparison changed card and server process while neither of its own noise controls did, so its attribution rests on the cross-cell argument alone. CORRECTED 2026-07-30: the operator-facing summary previously claimed EVERY A/A pair spanned both cards. It did not -- tu93's head-arm A/A ran head and headb on the same card AND the same server PID. The base-arm replicate added on review partly closes that gap for tu93: base and baseb ran on the same card but in DIFFERENT server processes (789471 vs 855597, i.e. a fresh model load and a fresh prompt cache) and came back byte-identical, so the process/cache channel is controlled there even though the cross-card channel is not. The other three attributable cells (tn36, tr87, vc33) have base-arm A/A pairs that crossed BOTH cards and BOTH server processes.

direct_test_of_the_operators_question.dependence_disclosure_the_two_rows_are_n: Fisher's exact test assumes the two rows are independent samples. They are not. The A/B arm is base-vs-head and the A/A arm is head-vs-headb, so BOTH rows contain the ENTIRE head arm -- the same 8 head runs appear on both sides of the table. A head run that happened to be unusual perturbs both rows together. The p-values below are therefore approximate in an unquantified direction and should be read as an effect-size sanity check, not as a formal test.
direct_test_of_the_operators_question.interpretation_guide: a small p means the code perturbs the agent more than the harness perturbs itself. A p above 0.05 at this n does NOT mean the code is inert -- it means this many cells cannot separate the two rates; see n_cells_to_separate_ab_rate_from_aa_floor_per_arm. The per-cell MECHANISM evidence (see vc33_goal_predicate_regression_replicated_across_two_probes) is independent of this p-value and does not depend on it.

n_needed_if_the_observed_rates_hold.conclusion: SEVEN usable cells per arm suffice for the direct question, against the TWELVE the sign-test gate needs. The operator's question is answerable at roughly half the cost of the pre-flight's own gate.
n_needed_if_the_observed_rates_hold.note: computed BEFORE the grid finished, so it is a pre-registered expectation rather than a post-hoc rationalisation of whatever n happened to land. Assumes A/B 0.5 and A/A 0.0, the rates measured over the first four games.

primary_attributable_consistent.note: uses the ATTRIBUTABLE numerator -- the same count the rest of the artifact headlines -- rather than the raw perturbed count.

primary_matched_cells_only.note: cells usable in BOTH arms, so the two rates are measured on the SAME cells. This is the primary figure.

direct_test_of_the_operators_question.question: has anything shipped changed the live agent's behaviour AT ALL -- i.e. is the A/B perturbation rate greater than the A/A noise floor?

upper_bound_raw_unmatched_cell_sets.note: the ORIGINAL table. Raw perturbed count, unmatched cell sets. Reported as a clearly-labelled UPPER BOUND on the evidence, not as the headline: it is the most favourable of the three tables available.

direct_test_of_the_operators_question.which_field_is_the_headline: primary_matched_cells_only. The two legacy fields immediately above are the original unmatched computation, retained unchanged so the correction is auditable rather than silently overwritten -- do NOT cite them.
direct_test_of_the_operators_question.why_not_the_sign_test: the sign test in preflight_verdict answers the pre-flight's own gate ('could a 12-cell banked-levels grid reach alpha'), which is a different and stricter question. Reporting only that gate would understate what these data show about the question actually asked.

duration_s_provenance: wall clock from the first driver log line to the last cell written, across BOTH drivers (the 8-game A/B+A/A grid and the 4-cell base-arm A/A replicate). grid_design_finding_the_threshold_assume.claim: the '6 one-way discordant pairs out of 12 cells' threshold silently assumes all 12 cells YIELD a usable observation. On this path some do not, so the effective denominator is smaller than 12 and the required attributable RATE is higher than the 50% the '6 of 12' framing suggests.
grid_design_finding_the_threshold_assume.confirmed_in_this_run_not_only_predicted: sc25's A/A replicate hit the 1500s hard timeout and was SIGTERM'd mid-induction (status blocked_hard_timeout_sigterm, 26 actions of partial trace), so sc25's A/A is TRUNCATION_ONLY and the cell is excluded from the A/A denominator. Its base and head cells took 1100s and 1150s against a 1200s wall cap -- i.e. the cell was already at the edge, and the third arm fell off it. The truncation risk is therefore not a prediction transplanted from the retention grid; it materialised here, on the FOURTH game, before the grid even reached the games known to be slower.
grid_design_finding_the_threshold_assume.consequence: if k of 12 cells are truncation-affected, the sign test needs 6 of (12-k) usable cells to be attributably perturbed. At k=2 that is 60%; at k=5 (the retention grid's rate) it is 86%, which no plausible treatment reaches. So a 12-game grid on the slow games is close to arithmetically undesignable, independent of the treatment.
grid_design_finding_the_threshold_assume.evidence_from_the_prior_retention_grid: in results/arc_engine_retention_20260729, cn04 and r11l were BOTH_TRUNCATED (both arms cut off at 26-28 of a 400-action budget) and lp85, ls20, su15 were TRUNCATION_ONLY -- 5 of 12 cells truncation-affected, leaving 7 usable. The pre-flight correctly EXCLUDES those as missing observations rather than scoring them zero, which is right -- but it means the grid never had 12 chances.
grid_design_finding_the_threshold_assume.recommendation: size the grid by USABLE cells, not scheduled cells: either drop the games that reliably truncate at this wall-clock cap, raise the cap for them specifically, or schedule enough extra games that the expected usable count clears the threshold. This is a design fix, not a re-analysis -- no amount of care in the analysis can recover power the schedule never had.
grid_design_finding_the_threshold_assume.status_in_this_run: see ab_class_counts / n_truncation_affected for the running totals. Reported as a design finding regardless of this run's outcome, because the arithmetic gap exists whether or not this particular grid tripped over it.

headline_why: the probe did not finish and the cells still outstanding could still carry the ceiling to the threshold. This is NOT evidence the treatment is inert.

instrument_cross_check_external_vs_head_._comparator_bug_found_on_review_and_fixe: the first version compared the STRING "None" against a genuine absent payload on every data-less action (external `ACTION7|None` vs native `{"action":7}`), so it reported _all_head_cells_agree=false with mismatches at index 1-2 while the traces were in fact identical. Absent payloads are now normalised to None on both sides, and the check now covers the headb cells too. If this field is false, the instrument really does disagree with the shipped recorder and nothing else in the artifact should be trusted.

instrumentation_gap_in_this_probe_a_time.fix: have the SIGTERM handler write the `pre` witness dict alongside the partial trace -- it is already fully populated by the time the action loop starts.
instrumentation_gap_in_this_probe_a_time.observed: headb/sc25 was SIGTERM'd at the 1500s hard timeout, so its record has e3_dir_resolved=None and no witnesses -- visible in fairness_witnesses_per_cell, where that cell is absent.
instrumentation_gap_in_this_probe_a_time.what: the cell's SIGTERM handler writes a MINIMAL record -- arm, game, seed, status, elapsed_s_at_kill, and the partial action trace. It does NOT write the fairness witnesses (e3_dir_resolved, effective sampler seed, imported module paths, observed model path / n_ctx, server exe and per-PID VRAM), because those live in the `pre` dict the handler does not close over.
instrumentation_gap_in_this_probe_a_time.why_it_does_not_change_this_verdict: a truncated cell is excluded as a missing observation, so it contributes to neither the numerator nor the denominator of any rate here.
instrumentation_gap_in_this_probe_a_time.why_it_is_still_a_gap: the TRUNCATION_ONLY classification itself is computed FROM that partial trace (the prefix comparison), so a claim is being made about a trace whose provenance the record cannot confirm -- we cannot verify from the artifact that the killed cell was running the arm it says it was, with the seed it says it used. Small here; it would matter if a truncated cell's prefix were ever load-bearing.

instrumentation_shims_and_why_each_is_fa.action_trace: HEAD grew a native ProgressResult.action_trace (29daa97b0); the baseline has none -- the measuring instrument was itself part of the shipped work. Rather than backport it, the probe cell wraps E3AgentPolicy.next_move and records decisions itself: ONE instrument, defined outside both checkouts, applied identically to both arms, so a trace cannot differ because one arm records more carefully. HEAD's native trace is captured separately as a cross-check.
instrumentation_shims_and_why_each_is_fa.arm_config: the baseline's ARM_CONFIGS has no frozen_gemma_pin entry and raised KeyError on the first launch attempt. The cell writes the config literal into ARM_CONFIGS on BOTH arms rather than falling back to `frozen` (which both define, byte-identically, but which runs under /no_think -- not the live gemma pin). Both apply_arm implementations were verified to read the same six keys.
instrumentation_shims_and_why_each_is_fa.policy_game_id: HEAD's run_bounded_progress accepts policy_game_id; the baseline's does not. Passing it to HEAD alone would let the baseline's policy see the real game id and route on per-game prior knowledge while HEAD's could not -- a behavioural confound far larger than anything under test. The wrapper forces the anonymized id on both arms instead.
instrumentation_shims_and_why_each_is_fa.sampler_seed: sampling_seed (added by 0da7f75ad, i.e. INSIDE the span under test) is patched into the base worktree from p2/seed_shim.patch. Verified: identical function body by AST comparison, and 4 call sites on each side. CONSEQUENCE, stated rather than buried: the A/B measures the 25-commit span MINUS the seed plumbing. That plumbing is default-OFF measurement infrastructure, not a behaviour change, so excluding it is the correct scoping -- but it IS an exclusion.

sampler_seed_asymmetry_found_and_closed.method_note: recorded because the CHECK is the transferable part: comparing call COUNTS passed and would have hidden this. Comparing (enclosing function, argument) pairs caught it.
sampler_seed_asymmetry_found_and_closed.what_i_found: counting call sites (4 vs 4) was NOT sufficient. Comparing the ENCLOSING FUNCTION and the ARGUMENT of every `sampling_seed(...)` call shows the arms differ on one of the three seeded paths: HEAD calls `sampling_seed(attempt)` inside `_chat_complete_request`, while the shimmed baseline calls `sampling_seed(0)` there. So on retries (attempt>0) via the chat-template route the two arms would sample with DIFFERENT seeds -- exactly the confound the seeding exists to remove.
sampler_seed_asymmetry_found_and_closed.what_would_make_it_bite: any future probe that enables `use_chat_template` (e.g. to run a Qwen or ThinkingCap generator, which need the assistant-turn structure) MUST NOT reuse this seed shim as-is: on retries the arms would diverge for seeding reasons rather than code reasons, and the divergence would look like a treatment effect. Verify the enclosing-function/argument pairs, not the call count.
sampler_seed_asymmetry_found_and_closed.why_it_is_INERT_for_this_probe: both call sites are guarded by `if self.use_chat_template:`, and `use_chat_template: bool = False` is the dataclass default on BOTH arms (base line 3688, HEAD line 4141). The probe cell never sets it. So the chat-template route is not taken in any cell here, and the asymmetric call is unreachable. The two paths that ARE used -- `generate(attempt)` and `complete_text(0)` -- are identical on both arms.
sampler_seed_asymmetry_found_and_closed.why_the_shim_could_not_match_it: base's `_chat_complete_request` has no `attempt` parameter at all; HEAD's signature is `(..., attempt: int = 0)`. That plumbing was added inside the span under test, so no patch to the baseline could replicate it without importing part of the treatment.

known_limits_do_not_over_read: the BASE-ARM noise floor covers only the 4 cells that carried the attributable finding, not all 12. Every other cell has NO base-side determinism witness, so its A/B classification rests on the head arm's floor alone -- the exact gap this replicate was added to close, closed only where it mattered most.

attributable-to-the-SPAN and attributable-to-INDUCTION are different numbers and the second is much smaller. Only a cell where a plan was found can evidence the induction-side work; a pre-induction explore reordering is a real behavioural difference but says nothing about what this session shipped. Cite the induction number when the claim is about the session's fixes.

the Fisher rows are NOT independent: the A/B arm is base-vs-head and the A/A arm is head-vs-headb, so the same 8 head runs appear on both sides of every table. Read the p-values as an effect-size sanity check, not as a formal test.

PYTHONHASHSEED is not pinned on either arm, so per-process str/bytes hash randomisation is a live nondeterminism channel that the seeding does not close. The A/A replicates MEASURE its consequences on the probed cells rather than eliminating it; a cell without an A/A replicate has that channel uncontrolled.

head is 2.5-3.1x slower than base on the two cells where the treatment demonstrably activates (vc33, tn36) while being faster on two others. Perturbing the agent is not the same as improving it, and the scored metric is efficiency-sensitive -- see wall_time_and_truncation_asymmetry.

budget=60 and max_inductions=1: a change that acts only at induction #2/#3, or only after a level-up deep in a 400-action run, is INVISIBLE here. An INERT verdict therefore means 'not detectably perturbing within 60 actions and 1 induction', NOT 'inert in all regimes'.
the A/B excludes the sampler-seed plumbing (see instrumentation_shims), because holding the sampler constant is what makes attribution possible at all.

a PERTURBS verdict would mean only that the treatment perturbs enough cells for the planned sign test to be ABLE to reach significance. Perturbation is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for discordance on banked levels.
12 cells is ONE seed per game. A per-game seed replicate would separate game-specific from seed-specific perturbation; it was not run.
this is a PRE-FLIGHT, not a banked-levels measurement. It answers 'did the code reach the agent', never 'did the code help'.

see ab_divergence_locations: a perturbed cell whose first divergence lands before the ~24-transition explore budget is spent cannot have been caused by an induction-side change, because no world model has been proposed yet. Such a cell still counts as attributable perturbation (it IS a behavioural difference under a determinism-witnessed cell) but it does NOT evidence the induction-side fixes.

the_standing_gate_verbatim.text: NO quota until offline transfer > 0.08 AND beats best prior submitted run
the_standing_gate_verbatim.why_it_is_doubly_anchored: the first clause is anchored to the MODAL score (0.08, seen three times) and the second to the SINGLE-OBSERVATION maximum (0.12). If 0.12 is variance around a 0.08 level, the second clause asks a new run to beat a lucky draw rather than to beat the system's actual level -- so it can be failed by a genuine improvement and passed by noise.

methodology_note: best_reachable_p_strict and best_reachable_p_charitable are a BOUND PAIR, not two independent measurements: the charitable ceiling is DEFINED as the strict ceiling plus the number of truncation-affected A/B cells, so the two are equal WHENEVER that slack term is zero, and differ by exactly that term otherwise. In THIS run the A/B truncation count is 1 (su15, whose base arm hit the 1200s soft wall cap after 28 agreeing actions), so the ceilings are 4 and 5 and the p-values are 0.125 and 0.0625 -- NOT equal. The TAUTOLOGY flag that fired on earlier 6-game builds of this artifact was a structural false positive of exactly this bound-pair shape, and it CLEARED ITSELF on the final build once su15's truncation made the slack non-zero, which is the proof that it was structural rather than a real coincidence. NO number here has been altered to satisfy a linter; see defects_found_in_the_instrument_while_using_it for the recommended carve-out.

retrospective_validation_of_the_instrume.note: reproduced live in this session, so the instrument's stated refusal is checked rather than cited.

structural_channel_check.RETRACTION_the_guaranteed_identical_clai: the first version of this field said that on a cell where NEITHER arm found a plan 'the two arms are GUARANTEED to emit identical traces however differently they induced'. That is false, and this artifact's own numbers falsified it: tn36, tr87 and tu93 are ALL in cells_with_no_plan_on_either_arm AND all three are classified PERTURBED, diverging at action index 2-3. Both facts were stated and never reconciled. The claim was wrong because it conflated the INDUCTION channel with the ACTION STREAM: a plan is the only route from an induction-side change to the actions, but the EXPLORE stream runs whether or not a plan is ever found, and a change to hashing, dedup or tie-breaking reorders it directly. The correct statement is narrower: on a no-plan cell the INDUCTION channel is closed, so any perturbation observed there is NOT evidence for the induction-side fixes -- it is evidence that SOMETHING in the 25-commit span reordered exploration.
structural_channel_check.how_to_read_the_two_counts: attributable_to_the_SPAN counts every cell where the A/B perturbed AND both arms were witnessed deterministic on that cell -- it answers 'did the 25-commit span change the live agent'. attributable_to_INDUCTION is the subset where a plan was found on at least one arm, i.e. where an induction-side change COULD have reached the actions -- it answers 'did the induction fixes change the live agent'. The second number is the one that speaks to what this session actually shipped, and it is much smaller. Reporting only the first would let explore-order reshuffling masquerade as the induction work paying off.
structural_channel_check.why_this_matters: every commit in the span acts on INDUCTION, and an induction-side change can reach the ACTION STREAM only through a PLAN. On a cell where NEITHER arm found a plan the induction channel is closed, so INERT there means 'the induction gate rejected every candidate on both arms', i.e. the bottleneck is UPSTREAM of everything shipped, NOT 'the fixes are worthless' -- and PERTURBED there means the perturbation came from somewhere OTHER than induction. On a plan-found cell the channel was open, so INERT is the much stronger claim and PERTURBED is the only kind of evidence that speaks to the induction fixes.

the_question: Every measurement this session tested ONE intervention in isolation and each came back inert or underpowered. But the fixes COMPOSE. Has anything shipped changed the live agent's behaviour AT ALL? That had never been asked.
title: Has anything the session shipped changed the live ARC agent at all? Composite treatment-activation pre-flight, HEAD vs 8441055c0

class_1_pre_induction_explore_reordering.downstream_effect_measured: none on these cells: tn36 and tr87 both end with plans=0, levels_gained=0 and the SAME total_actions on both arms (25/25 and 26/26). The change is real and attributable but does not reach any endpoint here.
class_1_pre_induction_explore_reordering.plausible_source_NOT_tested: a change to a hash, dedup key, tie-break or iteration order would produce exactly this signature, and 4f7e5f55a ('the search's dedup key') is in the span. Stated as a HYPOTHESIS: this probe compares the whole span at once and cannot attribute to a single commit. Bisecting it would be cheap.
class_1_pre_induction_explore_reordering.what: on STALL-triggered cells the arms diverge very early -- tn36 at action index 3, tr87 at index 2 -- which is before the 24-transition explore budget is spent and therefore before any world model exists. The divergence is a re-ordering over the SAME candidate click targets (tn36: Jaccard 1.0 on the distinct action set, identical multiset membership, different counts).

class_2_post_induction_plan_loss.downstream_effect_measured: levels_gained ties at 1, so a levels-only endpoint is blind; actions_to_first_solve moves by +5 with ZERO variance across six replicate runs. On an efficiency-sensitive metric that is a regression.
class_2_post_induction_plan_loss.what: on the one cell whose induction is LEVEL-UP-triggered and where a plan existed to lose (vc33), the goal predicate goes satisfiable -> unsatisfiable, the length-1 plan disappears, two extra refinement rounds are burned, and actions_to_first_solve goes 10 -> 15.

two_distinct_perturbation_classes_emerge.why_the_distinction_matters: collapsing them into '3 of 5 cells perturbed' would suggest a broad behavioural shift. The honest reading is narrower and more useful: the span makes a cosmetic-looking early ordering change nearly everywhere, and ONE substantive regression on the one cell where the targeted mechanism could actually act.

THE_EFFICIENCY_REGRESSION_this_is_the_st.correction_to_my_own_earlier_framing: I first wrote that a banked-levels grid 'would have scored this a TIE', implying the regression had no measurable cost. That is true of the LEVEL count and FALSE of the scored metric. Checking actions_to_first_solve shows a clean, fully reproducible efficiency regression, and ARC-AGI-3's scoring is efficiency-sensitive. Correcting rather than rewording, because the earlier phrasing understated the finding.
THE_EFFICIENCY_REGRESSION_this_is_the_st.reading: SIX runs across TWO independently-built probes, TWO independent sampler seeds and THREE commits, and the numbers are IDENTICAL within each side of the f9a458e87 boundary: 10 actions to first solve before it, 15 after. A 50% efficiency regression on this cell, with zero variance across replicates. levels_gained is 1 in all six runs, so a levels-only endpoint sees nothing.
THE_EFFICIENCY_REGRESSION_this_is_the_st.still_not_claimed: that this generalises. It is ONE game. Whether the same +5 appears on other level-up-reinduction games is unmeasured, and the probe's other cells (stall-triggered, no plan) cannot speak to it -- see observation_window_how_much_of_each_trace_is_downstream_of_the_induction.
THE_EFFICIENCY_REGRESSION_this_is_the_st.why_it_matters_for_the_score: the competition metric is efficiency-sensitive (actions consumed count against the score), so a reproducible +5 actions-to-first-solve is a SCORED regression on this game, not merely an internal one. That makes it a materially different finding from 'the fixes are inert'.

vc33_goal_predicate_regression_replicate.claim: the composite span contains a REPRODUCIBLE goal-predicate regression, localized to commit f9a458e87, that a banked-levels grid would have scored as a TIE.
vc33_goal_predicate_regression_replicate.cost_measured: a length-1 plan replaced by NO plan plus two extra LLM refinement rounds, and 4 extra actions (13 -> 17).
vc33_goal_predicate_regression_replicate.counterexample_text_from_the_run: the reachable set was searched exhaustively (frontier empty) and the goal was never true, so this predicate is unreachable under this engine

evidence.note: byte-identical to head, so the regression is deterministic, not a draw

vc33_goal_predicate_regression_replicate.localization: 8441055c0 and aa8a38e31 (f9a458e87's parent) both plan; f9a458e87 and HEAD both fail to plan with the same `degenerate_goal_predicate` counterexample. Four runs across TWO independent sampler seeds and two separately-built probes agree, so this is not a sampling artifact. The regression sits in f9a458e87 -- the commit whose stated purpose was to STOP penalising correct predicates.
vc33_goal_predicate_regression_replicate.not_claimed: that this regression costs banked levels anywhere. On vc33 it demonstrably does not -- both arms reach level 1. Whether it costs levels on a game where exploration cannot substitute for the plan is UNMEASURED. Nor is it claimed that f9a458e87 is a net regression: it fixed penalisation of correct predicates in three places, and this probe measures one game.
vc33_goal_predicate_regression_replicate.two_causes_this_probe_CANNOT_separate: (a) THE GATE GOT STRICTER -- f9a458e87 changed goal-predicate handling and now rejects a predicate the parent accepted; or (b) THE ENGINE GOT DIFFERENT -- head induced a different world model (its `retention_best_round_signal` is 1.0 where base records none) and the goal is genuinely unreachable inside THAT engine, so the gate is reporting honestly. The run's own diagnostics support (b) being possible: `termination: queue_exhausted` with `frontier_remaining: 0` means the reachable set was searched EXHAUSTIVELY rather than truncated by budget, which is the gate behaving correctly on whatever engine it was given. Separating the two needs the base engine replayed through head's gate and vice versa -- a cheap offline experiment, and the right next step. Until then the BEHAVIOURAL claim (base plans, head does not, reproducibly) stands, and the CAUSAL claim does not.
vc33_goal_predicate_regression_replicate.why_an_endpoint_grid_would_have_missed_i: both arms still reached level 1 by exploring, so levels_gained is 1 on both and a banked-LEVELS sign test scores this cell a TIE -- a discordant pair it never sees. The agent nonetheless lost its plan. This is the concrete case for the trace being the right instrument and a levels-only endpoint being the wrong one.

verdict_mapper_was_tested_and_two_of_my_.bug_1_i_tested_a_paraphrase_not_the_code: the verdict logic was inline in main(), so my first branch test was a hand-copied reimplementation of it. My copy silently OMITTED the CANNOT_ATTRIBUTE branch and therefore reported INERT on a scenario the real code handles correctly -- an error in the direction of understating a finding. Fix: extracted `_headline()` so the real branch order is the thing under test.
verdict_mapper_was_tested_and_two_of_my_.bug_2_INERT_on_zero_usable_observations: with the real function under test, a grid where EVERY cell was truncation-affected returned INERT. Truncated cells are missing observations, so that is a claim with no data behind it -- the exact missing-vs-zero error this pre-flight exists to prevent, committed inside its own verdict mapper. Not hypothetical: cn04 and r11l truncate reliably at ~27 actions on this path. Fix: a NO_USABLE_OBSERVATIONS verdict that fires before INERT can.
verdict_mapper_was_tested_and_two_of_my_.bug_3_fairness_audit_read_an_ABSENT_witn: the same missing-vs-zero error a THIRD time, now in the fairness audit. It compared each witness field across all present arms, so headb/sc25 -- SIGTERM'd before its witness dict was written -- contributed None as if it were a third, differing value. The audit reported FIVE fairness violations on sc25 (sampler seed, arm config, model path, n_ctx, policy id) when base and head agreed exactly on every one. Unfixed it would have looked like the arms were misconfigured and would have undermined the whole result, on a cell excluded from the analysis anyway. Fix: compare only arms that RECORDED the field; report absent witnesses under _witness_absent_not_a_mismatch as a coverage gap.
verdict_mapper_was_tested_and_two_of_my_.bug_4_the_instrument_cross_check_compara: found by REVIEW, not by me, and it is the SAME missing-vs-present error a FOURTH time. The external/native trace comparator normalised a data-less action to the four-character STRING "None" on one side (`ACTION7|None`) and to a genuine absent value on the other (`{"action":7}`), so it reported _all_head_cells_agree=false with mismatches at action index 1-2 -- INSIDE the region where this artifact's class-1 divergences live -- while the prose elsewhere correctly said the two recorders agree action-for-action. The prose was right and the FIELD was wrong, which is the worse way round: a reader checking the claim against the data would have concluded the instrument was unfaithful exactly where the finding sits. Fixed by normalising absent payloads on both sides; the check now covers 14 head+headb cells and all agree. The pattern of four independent instances in one session is itself the finding: this codebase's comparators default to treating 'no value' as 'a value', and that default has been wrong every single time.
verdict_mapper_was_tested_and_two_of_my_.why_recorded: the mapper decides the headline, so an untested mapper makes the headline unfalsifiable. Recording the bugs I found in my OWN analysis code rather than quietly fixing them, because a reader judging this artifact needs to know the verdict logic was adversarially exercised, not just run once on the happy path.

wall_time_and_truncation_asymmetry.correction_to_the_review_that_prompted_t: the review stated '2 of the 3 A/B truncation events dropped the HEAD cell (cd82 head SIGTERM, sc25 head)'. Checked against the cells: the three truncation events in the grid are head/cd82 (hard 1500s SIGTERM), headb/sc25 (hard 1500s SIGTERM) and base/su15 (soft 1200s wall cap, status ok with result.timed_out=True). sc25's truncated arm is headb, which is in the A/A arm and costs an A/A observation, not an A/B one. So of the TWO A/B truncation events, one dropped head (cd82) and one dropped base (su15) -- symmetric, not head-selecting. The broader point survives in a weaker form: 2 of the 3 events across the whole grid landed on the head-arm CODE (head and headb), and the two cells where head is >=2x slower are exactly the cells where the treatment demonstrably activates.
wall_time_and_truncation_asymmetry.scored_efficiency_flag: vc33 137.2s -> 428.5s (3.1x) and tn36 259.1s -> 639.9s (2.5x) are a candidate SCORED-EFFICIENCY REGRESSION, to be read alongside vc33's actions_to_first_solve 10 -> 15. The ARC scoring metric is efficiency-sensitive, so 'perturbs the agent' is not the same as 'improves the agent' and this artifact claims only the former. NOT claimed: that the wall-time cost transfers to the scored submission stack, which runs a different generator on different hardware.

which_preflight_verdict_governs: preflight_verdict_full, which passes BOTH arms' A/A floors to the module. The ..._ORIGINAL_... field is the single-arm computation this artifact shipped before review, kept verbatim so the correction can be checked rather than taken on trust. Where the two disagree, the two-arm one is right by construction: it requires each arm to have been separately witnessed deterministic on the cell being attributed.
why_this_baseline: 8441055c0 is the first commit after the Qwen3.6-27B -> gemma-4-31B-it inducer migration, so the GENERATOR MODEL IS HELD CONSTANT and the A/B isolates the CODE. a2222320c was rejected as the primary baseline precisely because it spans that model swap: it would perturb every trace trivially and say nothing about the code.
why_two_attributable_counts: n_attributable_perturbed is the ORIGINAL count, which required only the head arm's A/A -- retained unchanged so the correction is auditable rather than silently overwritten. n_attributable_under_both_arm_floors is the CORRECT one and is what every verdict in this artifact now uses: a cell counts only when the A/B perturbed AND both arms were separately witnessed to repeat themselves on that same cell.
